Installation, long-outage and complete process-level acceptance. Explicit pre-seal mTLS pulls preserve staged objects across two authorized hops and bridge reopen, with signed closure and independent recovery verified at the final receiver. Paired source writes queue one confirmed-object import after a transient handoff failure, and the worker resumes it on the same authorized route without a new source upload. SIGKILL after durable queue admission preserves the original request for replay. After a second SIGKILL after durable object write, the recipient resumes the queued import and restores the signed generation with the bridge offline. The recipient can durably rebind an exact queued object to an admitted origin after policy withdraws the previous route. A queued import can also carry one pre-admitted alternate and finish after reopening when the primary is offline, while a withdrawn alternate stays unavailable. During recovery of a two-copy ACTIVE route, the source can select the superseded holder as an alternate after it confirms the exact staged object. The new pair still decides publication, and the current recipient policy decides whether it can use that alternate. Full chain scheduling, alternate selection outside this replacement flow and additional process crash boundaries remain open. The offline CLI reports declared routes and unreachable holders, compares peer graphs and domain trust, checks all expected holder and transit documents against one signed domain reference, and reports exact autonomous rule mismatches and peer revision lag. Installed topology, runtime permissions and connectivity acceptance remain open.
